reading.body:
Wipro's public record shows a services company with 738 granted patents, none of them about AI compute, buildings, or power.

The patent sample is the clearest signal. The five most recent grants cover hydraulic valve arrangements, a heavy construction machine actuator, a hydraulic cylinder, vehicle device onboarding, and a vehicle safety mechanism. That is industrial and automotive engineering, not data centers or accelerators. A company describing itself as AI-powered is not, on this evidence, building the physical layer that AI scaling depends on.

The filings are eight 6-K submissions between late June and late July 2026, the routine disclosure cadence of a foreign private issuer on the NYSE. They establish that Wipro reports regularly and is listed. They do not contain, in this data, any capacity, power, or capital expenditure figures.

What this does not cover is the substance of Wipro's AI work. The profile text is the company's own general description, and the data lists no AI products, no MCP servers, and no lawsuits. Nothing here measures how much AI compute Wipro consumes or resells, which is the number that would connect it to the grid constraint. The absence of that number is a gap in the record, not a finding about the company.

profile_text.body:
Wipro is a public company traded under the ticker WIT, according to its registration record. Its own website describes it as a consulting-led and AI-powered technology services and consulting company. The company says it blends consulting and AI expertise across design, engineering and operations to accelerate business transformation and deliver future-ready technology, and describes itself as a global leader in that work.

The material available does not list specific AI products, MCP servers, or lawsuits for Wipro. The site's description is general, covering consulting and AI expertise applied across design, engineering and operations rather than naming individual offerings.
